is OD counted for 75 percent attendance
documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND INSTITUTIONAL MANDATE
Demo University actively fosters holistic student development through participation in competitive athletic events, national hackathons, technical symposiums, research conferences, and cultural festivals. This policy establishes official regulations governing the sanction of On-Duty (OD) attendance exemptions, ceiling limits, procedural approval workflows, and automated attendance adjustments.

2. JURISDICTION AND DEFINITIONS
2.1 On-Duty (OD) Attendance Exemption: An authorized excused absence granted to a registered student officially selected to represent Demo University in sanctioned external or campus-wide co-curricular and extracurricular events.
2.2 Attendance Factorization: Approved OD days are factored into AttendEdge attendance tracking engines as 'Excused Present', thereby safeguarding the candidate's statutory 75% attendance eligibility for Semester End Examinations (SEE).

3. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA AND SANCTIONED ACTIVITIES
3.1 Permissible Categories: OD absence may be sanctioned exclusively for:
  a) Inter-university sports tournaments endorsed by the University Sports Directorate.
  b) National and international technical hackathons, design symposiums, and competitive collegiate coding contests endorsed by Department Heads.
  c) Peer-reviewed academic conferences where the student is presenting an accepted research paper.
  d) Authorized university cultural festivals, leadership summits, or inter-collegiate debates coordinated by the Student Activity Centre.
3.2 Non-Permissible Categories: OD cannot be claimed for personal travel, family functions, private coaching, job interviews not coordinated through the Career Development Centre, or unapproved student-initiated trips.

4. STATUTORY CEILINGS AND LIMITATIONS
4.1 Semester Cap: On-Duty leave is strictly limited to a maximum of 10 working days per academic semester across all registered courses.
4.2 Non-Extendable Threshold: Absences exceeding the 10-day statutory ceiling cannot be categorized as On-Duty and will be recorded as unexcused absences in AttendEdge.

5. PROCEDURAL APPLICATION AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW (PROC-OD-SANCTION)
5.1 Pre-Event Application: The student must log an official OD Request ticket on ResolveDesk at least 3 working days prior to the commencement of the event, attaching the formal invitation brochure, selection letter, and scheduled travel itinerary.
5.2 Faculty Endorsement: The designated Faculty Coordinator (Sports Director, Club Mentor, or Project Guide) verifies the authenticity of the event and digitally endorses the application.
5.3 Executive Approval: The Dean of Student Affairs (DSA) reviews institutional merit and grants formal administrative sanction.
5.4 Post-Event Claim Submission: Within 5 working days of returning to campus, the student must upload the official Certificate of Participation / Attendance and a brief event report to the original ResolveDesk ticket.
5.5 Automated System Reconciliation: Upon post-event verification, AttendEdge automatically adjusts course attendance records for the approved dates from absent to 'Excused OD'.

documents.title: Student Grievance Redressal and Ombudsman Policy
audience: All Enrolled Students and Student Groups
retrieval_signals: escalate complaint to Dean of Student Welfare
protection against retaliation for filing complaint
documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND PRINCIPLES OF NATURAL JUSTICE
Demo University is committed to maintaining a transparent, fair, and responsive academic environment where student concerns are resolved expeditiously and impartially. This policy defines the statutory framework for redressing student grievances, establishing a three-tier escalation hierarchy, strict service-level agreements (SLAs), and non-retaliation protections.

2. SCOPE AND JURISDICTION
2.1 Cognizable Grievances: A formal grievance may be lodged regarding:
  a) Academic Irregularities: Arbitrary or discriminatory internal grading, denial of sanctioned On-Duty leave, or unnotified syllabus deviations.
  b) Administrative Deficiencies: Inordinate delays in publishing results, issuing bonafide letters, or processing fee adjustments and refunds.
  c) Campus Facilities & Services: Persistent failure in hostel maintenance, mess hygiene, transportation routes, or digital library access.
  d) Victimization and Harassment: Discrimination based on gender, caste, creed, regional origin, or physical disability.
2.2 Excluded Matters: Disciplinary sanctions imposed by the Proctorial Board and sexual harassment complaints (governed exclusively by the Internal Complaints Committee) fall outside the purview of this policy.

3. THREE-TIER ESCALATION HIERARCHY AND SLAS (PROC-GRIEVANCE-REDRESS)
3.1 Level 1 — Department Grievance Cell:
  a) Submission: The student logs a formal grievance ticket on ResolveDesk, categorizing the issue and attaching corroborating evidence.
  b) Operational SLA: The ticket routes automatically to the Department Grievance Officer, who must investigate and publish a formal resolution within 5 working days.
3.2 Level 2 — Central Student Grievance Redressal Committee:
  a) Escalation Trigger: If the candidate remains dissatisfied with the Level-1 determination, they may click 'Escalate to Level 2' within 48 hours of ticket closure.
  b) Operational SLA: Chaired by the Dean of Student Welfare (DSW), the Central Committee convenes a hearing with the student and concerned department within 10 working days.
3.3 Level 3 — Independent University Student Ombudsman:
  a) Apex Appeal: If the grievance remains unresolved at Level 2, the matter is referred to the Independent University Student Ombudsman, appointed by the Board of Management.
  b) Final Determination: The Ombudsman conducts independent inquiries and delivers a binding verdict within 20 working days.

4. STATUTORY WHISTLEBLOWER AND ANTI-RETALIATION PROTECTIONS
Any attempt by faculty, administrative personnel, or senior students to penalize, intimidate, lower internal marks, or retaliate against a student for filing a bona fide grievance is strictly prohibited and constitutes gross misconduct punishable by immediate administrative suspension.

documents.title: Zero-Tolerance Anti-Ragging and Harassment Policy

expulsion for ragging at Demo University
documents.content:
1. STATUTORY ZERO-TOLERANCE MANDATE
Demo University enforces absolute, unyielding zero tolerance against ragging, bullying, intimidation, hazing rituals, and physical or psychological harassment across all campus premises, hostels, transit buses, and off-campus student accommodation. This policy defines prohibited conduct, emergency reporting avenues, flying squad mobilization, and punitive consequences.

2. DEFINITION AND FORMS OF RAGGING
Ragging constitutes any act by any student, whether individually or collectively, that creates an intimidating, hostile, or humiliating environment. Prohibited acts include:
2.1 Psychological & Verbal: Indulging in rowdy speech, teasing, using abusive epithets, forcing juniors to perform embarrassing acts, or addressing juniors disrespectfully.
2.2 Physical Hazing: Coerced physical exercises, confinement to hostel rooms, forced consumption of substances, sleep deprivation, or assault.
2.3 Financial Exploitation: Extorting money, demanding forced treats, or compelling juniors to complete academic assignments, lab records, or coding tasks.
2.4 Cyberbullying: Creating unauthorized social media pages, sharing humiliating memes, or sending intimidating messages over digital networks.

3. STATUTORY PREVENTIVE MEASURES
Every admitted undergraduate and postgraduate student and their parent/guardian must submit a digitally signed, verifiable Anti-Ragging Affidavit on UniCampus ERP during annual registration.

4. EMERGENCY REPORTING CHANNELS
Incidents of ragging may be reported 24 hours a day, 7 days a week through:
  a) The 24x7 University Anti-Ragging Emergency Phone Hotline.
  b) The Confidential & Anonymous Drop Module on ResolveDesk.
  c) Direct verbal or written reports to Residential Wardens, Security Personnel, or the Dean of Student Welfare.

5. INVESTIGATION AND EMERGENCY MOBILIZATION WORKFLOW (PROC-ANTI-RAGGING-INVEST / REL-011)
5.1 Instant Squad Mobilization: Upon receipt of a complaint, the Anti-Ragging Flying Squad mobilizes immediately. Plainclothes vigilance officers secure the premises.
5.2 Victim Protection and Relocation: Within 24 hours, the victim is provided secure accommodation or transferred to a protected hostel annexe to guarantee safety.
5.3 Emergency Hearing: The Dean of Student Welfare convenes an emergency inquiry session of the Anti-Ragging Committee within 24 hours to examine witnesses and review CCTV footage.
5.4 Statutory Punitive Sanctions: If substantiated, the Vice-Chancellor ratifies immediate disciplinary measures:
  a) Immediate suspension from academic classes and laboratory sessions.
  b) Instant eviction from university hostels and debarment from campus.
  c) Permanent expulsion from Demo University and forfeiture of academic credits.
  d) Transmission of formal First Information Report (FIR) to local law enforcement for criminal prosecution under statutory anti-ragging legislation.

documents.content:
1. JURISDICTIONAL PURPOSE
Demo University maintains high standards of campus decorum, personal integrity, and community safety. This policy regulates behavioral ethics, establishes statutory prohibitions against hazardous contraband, mandates restitution for property damage, and defines Proctorial Board disciplinary inquiry procedures.

2. PROHIBITED BEHAVIORAL INFRACTIONS
2.1 Contraband Prohibitions: The possession, distribution, consumption, or trade of alcohol, tobacco, narcotics, hallucinogens, psychotropic substances, or weapons on campus premises, buses, or hostels is absolutely prohibited. Violation results in immediate interim suspension pending formal expulsion.
2.2 Physical Violence & Disorder: Engaging in brawls, assaults, intimidation, riots, or threatening faculty or staff warrants instant interim debarment and campus exclusion.
2.3 Damage to Institutional Estate: Willful vandalism or reckless breakage of laboratory instruments, IT servers, classroom furniture, or residential estate requires 100% financial restitution plus punitive fines.
2.4 Impersonation & Digital Infractions: Providing unauthorized credentials, forging administrative signatures, or circumventing biometric turnstiles constitutes severe misconduct.

3. PROCTORIAL INQUIRY PROCEDURAL PHASES (PROC-DISCIPLINE-INQUIRY)
3.1 Phase 1 — Incident Reporting: The reporting authority (Security, Warden, or Faculty) submits a detailed incident docket to the Office of Student Welfare within 24 hours.
3.2 Phase 2 — Show-Cause Notice: The Proctorial Board Secretariat issues an official show-cause summons detailing allegations and scheduling a hearing within 7 working days.
3.3 Phase 3 — In Camera Hearing: The student appears before the Board, reviews photographic, digital, and witness evidence, and submits a signed written statement.
3.4 Phase 4 — Deliberation and Sanction: The Board evaluates aggravating and mitigating factors, determining proportionate penalties:
  a) Formal Admonition & Mandatory Mentorship.
  b) Community Service (up to 40 hours).
  c) Disciplinary Fine and Financial Restitution.
  d) Academic Suspension (one to two semesters).
  e) Permanent Expulsion and Degree Revocation.
3.5 Phase 5 — Order Ratification: The University Registrar ratifies the disciplinary order, updating UniCampus ERP with an administrative block.

1. PURPOSE AND CO-CURRICULAR VISION
Clubs and Student Activities Council (DEPT-SAC) oversees student organizations at Demo University. Operating from the Student Activity Centre (SAC Building, Ground Floor), this policy regulates club registration, faculty mentorship, activity budget approvals, venue bookings, and branding integrity.

2. FORMATION AND RECOGNITION REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Membership Threshold: Every prospective student club must demonstrate a registered roster of at least 20 active matriculated students.
2.2 Compulsory Faculty Mentorship: A proposed club must secure written sponsorship from a full-time university faculty member who agrees to act as Faculty Club Mentor.
2.3 Annual Renewal: Registered clubs must re-apply for chartered status annually in August via the ClubSpace Portal, submitting updated rosters, leadership election minutes, and annual activity reports.

3. EVENT SANCTION AND VENUE ALLOTMENT WORKFLOW (PROC-CLUB-EVENT / REL-008)
3.1 Ten-Day Advance Notice: Club events, technical workshops, hackathons, and guest lectures must be formally submitted on ResolveDesk at least 10 working days prior to the planned date.
3.2 Review and Multi-Department Coordination: The event dossier must contain detailed schedules, faculty mentor sign-offs, line-item budgets, and guest credentials. The SAC Chair coordinates with:
  a) Campus Operations (DEPT-OPS) for auditorium seating, sound infrastructure, and power.
  b) Campus Security (DEPT-SEC) for visitor gate ingress passes and parking allocation.
  c) IT Services (DEPT-IT) for temporary event Wi-Fi SSIDs.
3.3 Formal Sanction: Upon administrative approval, SAC issues an official Event Sanction Letter, listing the activity on the official university calendar.

4. FINANCIAL AND BRANDING RESTRICTIONS
4.1 Prohibition of Unauthorized Collections: Collecting cash membership fees or unauthorized student contributions is strictly prohibited. Approved budgets are disbursed through the Finance Office.
4.2 Corporate Sponsorships: External corporate sponsorships or brand partnerships require prior financial vetting and written authorization from the Finance and Accounts Office.
4.3 University Branding: All digital flyers, banners, and social media handles must adhere to Demo University brand guidelines.

audience: All Enrolled Undergraduate and Postgraduate Students

documents.content:
1. ETHICAL FOUNDATION AND VALUES
Demo University cultivates a collegiate environment rooted in intellectual rigor, personal integrity, mutual respect, and civic responsibility. This Code of Conduct defines the core behavioral obligations governing every enrolled student across all academic departments, research hubs, residential quarters, and digital communication spaces.

2. ACADEMIC AND CLASSROOM CIVILITY
2.1 Respectful Engagement: Students must treat faculty, technical assistants, administrative officers, and fellow peers with courtesy and professional respect.
2.2 Instructional Decorum: Punctual arrival for lectures, laboratory sessions, and seminars is mandatory. Unauthorized use of personal smartphones, gaming devices, or non-educational browsing during instructional periods is prohibited.
2.3 Recording Restrictions: Recording video or audio of classroom lectures, lab briefings, or faculty interactions without the explicit prior written consent of the instructor constitutes an infringement of privacy and intellectual property.

3. COMMUNITY HARMONY AND SOCIAL MEDIA ETHICS
3.1 Freedom of Expression with Responsibility: Democratic discourse, intellectual critique, and peaceful dialogue are respected. However, assemblies obstructing academic quadrangles, blockading administrative doors, or causing noise pollution during instruction are forbidden.
3.2 Digital and Online Decorum: Circulating defamatory, harassing, obscene, or threatening content targeting university members on online discussion forums, chat groups, or social media platforms is a punishable offense.

4. PROPERTY STEWARDSHIP AND SECURITY COOPERATION
4.1 Campus Badge Display: Students must visibly wear their official Demo University RFID Smart ID card at all times while inside academic complexes, libraries, and transport transit points.
4.2 Safety and Compliance: Students must comply immediately with lawful security directives issued by campus vigilance personnel.

The Department of Student Affairs (DEPT-DSA) operates from the Student Activity Centre (SAC Building, 1st Floor). Headed by the Dean of Student Affairs, the department serves as the institutional advocate for holistic non-academic student life, co-curricular governance, student leadership empowerment, and institutional representation.

2.1 Extracurricular Approvals Desk: Evaluates and sanctions student participation in external hackathons, athletic championships, and academic competitions, processing official On-Duty (OD) leaves in accordance with POL-OD.
2.2 Student Leadership Council Liaison: Mentors the elected university student council, coordinates student representation across statutory university boards, and facilitates leadership workshops.
2.3 Orientation & Campus Life Unit: Designs and conducts annual orientation bootcamps for incoming freshmen cohorts and manages annual university cultural festivals.
2.4 Parent-Student Relations Section: Coordinates parent-faculty interactions, communicates institutional advisories, and provides liaison assistance for international and outstation families.

3.1 Public Service Windows: The Department of Student Affairs maintains daily open office hours from 10:00 AM to 01:00 PM and 02:30 PM to 04:30 PM, Monday through Friday.

1. REGULATORY ENFORCEMENT FRAMEWORK
This document details the operational enforcement mechanisms, investigative workflows, victim protection protocols, and punitive processes mandated under the Zero-Tolerance Anti-Ragging Policy (POL-ANTI-RAGGING) of Demo University.

2. STATUTORY MONITORING BODIES
2.1 Anti-Ragging Committee: High-level statutory panel chaired by the Vice-Chancellor and executed by the Dean of Student Welfare, comprising faculty proctors, hostel wardens, local police representatives, non-governmental youth advocates, and student cohort representatives.
2.2 Anti-Ragging Flying Squad: Operational rapid-response unit conducting unannounced night patrols across freshmen hostel corridors, dining halls, cafeteria corners, and campus perimeter grounds.

3. TWENTY-FOUR-HOUR EMERGENCY MOBILIZATION PROTOCOL (PROC-ANTI-RAGGING-INVEST / REL-011)
3.1 Initial Complaint Receipt: Complaints logged via the 24x7 phone hotline, ResolveDesk anonymous portal, or in person trigger an automated Priority-1 alert.
3.2 Immediate Victim Security: Within 24 hours, the Flying Squad secures the victim, relocating them to secure residential quarters with round-the-clock security.
3.3 Emergency Hearing: The Anti-Ragging Committee convenes a formal hearing within 24 hours of notification, examining witnesses, hostel access logs from CampusPass, and CCTV feeds.

4. STATUTORY PENALTIES AND LEGAL CONSEQUENCES
Upon establishing prima facie guilt, the university enforces immediate non-negotiable penalties: academic suspension, permanent hostel eviction, expulsion from Demo University, and formal transmission of incident dossiers to local law enforcement for statutory FIR registration.

1. ADMINISTRATIVE MANDATE AND STRUCTURE
The Proctorial Board Secretariat constitutes the primary judicial inquiry body for student conduct at Demo University. Operating under the Office of Student Welfare (Chanakya Bhavan, 3rd Floor, Wing B), the Board investigates code-of-conduct breaches, acts of violence, substance prohibitions, and examination malpractice cases referred by the Examination Cell.

2. COMPOSITION AND QUORUM
The Board is chaired by the Dean of Student Welfare (DSW) and comprises the Chief Proctor, four senior faculty proctors representing different academic schools, the Chief Security Officer, and the Chief Warden of Hostels. A quorum of four members is required for formal proceedings.

3. HEARING WORKFLOW AND TIME-BOUND SLA (PROC-DISCIPLINE-INQUIRY)
3.1 Show-Cause Notice: Within 48 hours of receiving an incident report, the Secretariat issues a formal show-cause summons detailing the alleged violations, witness statements, and scheduled hearing time.
3.2 Inquiry Turnaround: The inquiry process must conclude within 7 working days from the date of the formal report.
3.3 In Camera Proceedings: Hearings are conducted in camera. The student is entitled to examine all physical, digital, and documentary evidence and to present a written and verbal defense. Legal representation by outside advocates is not permitted during internal academic inquiries.

4. PENALTY SPECTRUM AND PROMULGATION
4.1 Range of Sanctions: The Board may recommend Admonition, Community Service, Disciplinary Fines, Academic Suspension, or Expulsion.
4.2 Promulgation: Recommendations are transmitted to the University Registrar, who issues the formal Disciplinary Order and applies corresponding administrative hold flags in UniCampus ERP.

documents.content:
1. STATUTORY OBJECTIVE AND INDEPENDENCE
These regulations govern the statutory functioning of the Student Grievance Redressal Committee and the Office of the University Ombudsman at Demo University, guaranteeing independent, transparent, and binding resolution of student grievances in compliance with institutional and national higher education standards.

2. THREE-LEVEL DISPUTE RESOLUTION ARCHITECTURE (PROC-GRIEVANCE-REDRESS)
2.1 Level 1 — Department Grievance Cell:
  - Composition: Head of Department, two senior professors, and a faculty counselor.
  - Jurisdiction: Course assessment issues, internal sessional mark disputes, instructor absences, and lab scheduling conflicts.
  - Binding SLA: Must investigate and post a written determination within 5 working days.
2.2 Level 2 — Central Student Grievance Redressal Committee:
  - Composition: Chaired by the Dean of Student Welfare (DSW), with three senior professors, the Registrar, and an elected student representative.
  - Jurisdiction: Inter-departmental disputes, appeals against Level-1 determinations, administrative delays, and campus discrimination.
  - Binding SLA: Convenes formal hearing and issues a resolution order within 10 working days.
2.3 Level 3 — University Student Ombudsman:
  - Independence: A distinguished retired jurist or eminent academic appointed by the Board of Management, operating independently of the executive university administration.
  - Jurisdiction: Final appellate authority reviewing unresolved Level-2 cases, procedural injustice, or systemic administrative failure.
  - Binding SLA: Convenes appellate hearings and issues final, binding recommendations within 20 working days.

3. APPELLATE PROCEDURE AND FINALITY
Determinations made by the Ombudsman are submitted to the Vice-Chancellor for formal implementation. No further administrative appeal lies within the university.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND PORTAL ACCESS
This procedural manual provides step-by-step instructions for matriculated students to submit, monitor, and escalate formal academic, administrative, facilities, and conduct grievances using the university's central ticketing platform, ResolveDesk (https://resolve.demo.edu.internal).

2. STEP-BY-STEP SUBMISSION PROCEDURE
2.1 Authentication: Log in to ResolveDesk using official Demo University single-sign-on credentials.
2.2 Category Selection: From the primary dashboard, select 'Submit New Grievance' and choose the appropriate domain:
  - Academic Grievance (grading discrepancies, attendance adjustments, syllabus coverage).
  - Hostel & Residential Life (room maintenance, mess hygiene, curfew disputes).
  - Finance & Accounts (scholarship adjustments, tuition refunds, fee holds).
  - Harassment & Student Welfare (discrimination, bullying, unfair treatment).
2.3 Docket Details: Fill out the structured grievance form:
  - Detailed subject summary.
  - Specific operational dates, involved personnel, course codes, or room numbers.
  - Specific redress sought.
2.4 Evidence Attachment: Attach supporting documentation (scanned marks sheets, payment receipts, correspondence, or photographs). File attachments are restricted to PDF, PNG, or JPEG formats up to 10 MB.
2.5 Ticket Generation: Click 'Submit'. The system automatically issues a unique tracking code (e.g. `GRV-2026-XXXXX`) and starts the 5-day SLA countdown timer.

3. TRACKING AND ESCALATION WORKFLOW (PROC-GRIEVANCE-REDRESS)
3.1 Progress Monitoring: Students can view case updates, assigned officer comments, and request status directly from the 'My Tickets' dashboard.
3.2 Escalation to Level 2: If the assigned Department Grievance Officer fails to resolve the issue within 5 working days, or if the student is dissatisfied with the proposed solution, the student must click the 'Escalate to Level 2' button within 48 hours of ticket closure. The ticket escalates directly to the Central Student Grievance Redressal Committee.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND LEADERSHIP MANDATE
The Class Representative (CR) system establishes an official communication bridge between student cohorts, faculty instructors, department leadership, and the Department of Student Affairs. This charter defines eligibility standards, election procedures, functional responsibilities, and behavioral boundaries.

2. ELIGIBILITY AND NOMINATION CRITERIA
To qualify for election or appointment as Class Representative, a candidate must simultaneously fulfill three mandatory prerequisites:
  a) Academic Merit: Possess a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 7.00 or higher.
  b) Backlog-Free Status: Maintain zero uncleared course backlogs ('F' or 'I' grades) across all completed semesters.
  c) Clean Disciplinary Record: Possess zero formal citations, disciplinary reprimands, or active inquiries before the Proctorial Disciplinary Board.

3. ELECTION AND TENURE
3.1 Election Window: Elections or nominations are coordinated by the Academic Program Coordinator within the first two weeks of the academic semester.
3.2 Balanced Representation: Each section selects one primary Class Representative and one Deputy Representative, ensuring balanced gender representation where practicable.
3.3 Term: Representatives serve for one academic year, subject to semester performance review.

4. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES AND JURISDICTION
4.1 Faculty Liaison: Communicating constructive cohort feedback to course instructors regarding pacing, assignment schedules, and tutorial needs.
4.2 Class Committee Participation: Attending statutory Department Class Committee meetings chaired by the HOD to review curriculum progress and exam timetables.
4.3 Facility Reporting: Logging immediate infrastructure tickets on ResolveDesk regarding classroom air conditioning, multimedia projection, or biometric edge sensor errors.

5. BOUNDARIES AND DISMISSAL PROTOCOLS
5.1 Explicit Prohibitions: Class Representatives possess no authority to reschedule official examinations, condone student absences, collect unauthorized monetary funds, or organize class walkouts ('mass bunks'). Organizing or encouraging an unauthorized mass boycott of classes results in instant revocation of CR status and referral to the Proctorial Board.
5.2 Recall Procedure: A CR may be removed by the HOD upon receipt of a no-confidence petition signed by at least two-thirds of the registered section or upon failing to maintain the 7.00 CGPA threshold.

documents.content:
1. OPERATIONAL PURPOSE AND FACILITY INFRASTRUCTURE
The Campus Health Centre operates from the Health & Wellness Pavilion (adjacent to the East Residential Enclave). Equipped with a 24-hour outpatient diagnostic clinic, 10 emergency observation beds, a licensed pharmacy, and an emergency response ambulance, this SOP governs outpatient consultations and the rigorous verification of external medical documentation.

2. OUTPATIENT CLINICAL SERVICES
2.1 General Consultation: The outpatient clinic is open daily from 08:00 AM to 08:00 PM for general primary healthcare, minor trauma dressings, diagnostic blood profiling, and pharmacy dispensing.
2.2 Emergency Care: Emergency triage and observation services operate 24 hours a day under the supervision of resident medical officers.

3. MEDICAL DOCUMENTATION VERIFICATION WORKFLOW (PROC-MED-COND / REL-004)
When a student is absent due to acute illness or hospitalization and seeks academic attendance condonation, the following sequential workflow is mandatory:
3.1 Step 1 — In-Person Presentation: Within 3 working days of resuming academic attendance, the student must visit the Medical Verification Desk carrying complete original hospital records: clinical case history, discharge summary, registered doctor prescriptions, and laboratory investigation receipts.
3.2 Step 2 — Physician Audit: The Senior Chief Medical Officer examines the patient, scrutinizes diagnostic dates against class absence dates, cross-verifies hospital registration numbers, and validates clinical authenticity.
3.3 Step 3 — Verification Slip Issuance: Upon authenticating the illness, the Medical Officer generates an official University Medical Verification Slip in HealthDesk featuring a unique digital verification code and medical stamp.
3.4 Step 4 — ResolveDesk Upload: The student uploads a scanned copy of the endorsed medical slip to ResolveDesk under 'Medical Leave Submission' to notify their Faculty Advisor and HOD.
3.5 Step 5 — Academic Transmission: The department endorses the verified medical slip and routes it to the Dean of Academic Affairs to adjust attendance calculations within the 65.0% to 74.9% condonation band.

4. INTEGRITY SURVEILLANCE
Forged, altered, or purchased medical certificates will be impounded immediately. The Senior Medical Officer will file a formal disciplinary complaint with the Proctorial Board, triggering automatic semester suspension.
